label: July 1918
headline: Ninety-Three Minutes
deck: Australians and Americans take Hamel; the Germans leave the Marne
caption: Tanks and infantry advance together through standing wheat near Hamel
body: On 4 July, Independence Day, Australian infantry with companies of Americans attack at Hamel, east of Amiens. Tanks go forward with them, aircraft drop ammunition to the forward troops, and every objective is taken in ninety-three minutes. General Monash's plan is studied all along the Allied front.

On the Marne the Allied counter-attack of 18 July drives on. Château-Thierry is retaken on 21 July, and the Germans give up the salient won in May, falling back to the Vesle; on 2 August the French re-enter Soissons.
In Moscow the German ambassador, Count Mirbach, is shot dead on 6 July by Left Socialist Revolutionaries who hope to bring back war with Germany.
A million American soldiers are now in France, and ten thousand more land every day.
briefs: Quentin Roosevelt, son of the former President, is killed in the air
Field Marshal Conrad is relieved of his command in Italy
A U-boat shells a tug and barges off Cape Cod
